title: Coherent small open ringed-site realization and exact restriction
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a finite commutative ring, and $\tau$ either the small etale or small pro-etale topology [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Choose small representatives in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For each open subscheme $U\subseteq T$, write $A_U$ for the constant sheaf of rings [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The functor $\iota_U:(V\to U)\mapsto(V\to T,V\to U)$ is an equivalence of sites $U_\tau\simeq T_\tau/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], identifying covering families in both directions. Under this equivalence there is a canonical isomorphism of ring sheaves $e_U:A_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T|_U$ which carries each constant section $a\in A$ to the same constant section. Module restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is the exact functor $r_U$ given by
$$ (r_U F)(V\to U)=F(V\to T),\qquad (r_U f)_{V\to U}=f_{V\to T}, $$
with scalar action transported along $e_U$. For $W\subseteq U\subseteq T$, the direct site equivalence and the successive site equivalences agree under relocalization $(T_\tau/U)/W\simeq T_\tau/W$. If $e_{W/U}:A_W\xrightarrow{\sim}A_U|_W$ denotes the corresponding coefficient comparison on $U$, then
$$ e_W=(e_U|_W)\circ e_{W/U}. $$
Consequently the canonical comparison $\eta_{W,U}:r_{W/U}r_U\xrightarrow{\sim}r_W$ of exact module functors is sectionwise the identity, including scalar actions and morphisms; these comparisons satisfy the identity and associativity laws for further nested opens.

proof.text: Work with the common bounded representatives of [def-weil-size-convention], before passage to skeleta. For the etale site, [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] makes $U\hookrightarrow T$ an object, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] gives precisely $\iota_U$ and preservation of covering families in both directions. For the pro-etale site, apply [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to the open subscheme $U$: its clause (1) gives the same object and arrow formulas and the same covering identification. Transfer these equivalences to the chosen small representatives. Thus both cases identify sheaves by precomposition with $\iota_U$; no change of universe is needed.

source.place: Tag 00XZ (section-localize); small pro-etale specialization: proetale.tex, Tag 098K (definition-big-small-proetale), and more-morphisms.tex, Tags 094T/0951; reuse the existing localization statements.

proof.text: Let $P_T$ be the constant ring presheaf with value $A$ and let $u_T:P_T\to A_T$ be its sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Its restriction to $T_\tau/U$ is literally the constant ring presheaf there. Apply [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] to $P_T$. After Step 1 its isomorphism is $e_U:A_U\simeq A_T|_U$, with $e_Uu_U=u_T|_U$. In particular it sends the constant section $a$ to the same constant section. The equivalence of sites preserves this sheafification description: a map from the constant presheaf into a sheaf on either side is exactly the same family of maps on the corresponding objects.

source.place: Tags 00XR (lemma-when-shriek), 00XZ (section-localize); ring-valued sheafification comparison and its unit identity as stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Restrict an $A_T$-module on the slice using [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], then use $\iota_U$ and $e_U$ to regard it as an $A_U$-module. This gives exactly $(r_UF)(V\to U)=F(V\to T)$ and $(r_Uf)_{V\to U}=f_{V\to T}$, with action $b\cdot x=e_U(b)x$. Restriction to the slice is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], applied to $\mathcal C=T_\tau$ and $\mathcal O=A_T$. The two subsequent changes are equivalences: their inverses use the inverse site equivalence and $e_U^{-1}$. Hence kernels and cokernels transfer by their universal properties, and exactness is preserved. This proves exactness of the specified $r_U$, rather than sectionwise surjectivity on arbitrary objects.

source.place: Tag 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site), section 03DH and Tag 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); restriction exactness in the cited module-adjunction theorem.

proof.text: For $W\subseteq U$, the relocalization of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] sends $((V\to U),V\to W)$ to $V\to W$; its inverse remembers the composite $V\to W\to U$. These are inverse on objects and arrows, and coverings are the same underlying families. Both direct and successive scheme-site identifications send $V\to W$ to $V\to T$ and leave its arrows unchanged. Thus their restrictions, including their sheafification units, agree under this relocalization.

source.place: Tag 03EH (lemma-relocalize), object formula and commutative triangle; ringed counterpart sites-modules.tex Tag 04IY (lemma-relocalize).

proof.text:
Use the unit identity of [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] on both $T$ and $U$. Under Step 4,
$$(e_U|_W)e_{W/U}u_W=(e_U|_W)(u_U|_W)=u_T|_W=e_Wu_W.$$
Since $A_W$ is the sheafification of its constant ring presheaf, uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $e_W=(e_U|_W)e_{W/U}$. This proves the coefficient cocycle on all sections, not just an equality tested on the global constants. For the identity inclusion the comparison has composite $u_U$ with the unit, so the same uniqueness makes it the identity.

source.place: Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), uniqueness, and Tag 03EH (lemma-relocalize); coefficient identity corresponding to sites-modules.tex Tag 04IY.

proof.text: For $V\to W$, both $r_{W/U}r_UF$ and $r_WF$ have the group $F(V\to T)$ and the same restriction maps. Their $A_W(V)$-actions are respectively $b\cdot x=(e_U|_W)(e_{W/U}(b))x$ and $b\cdot x=e_W(b)x$, equal by Step 5. The identity on this group therefore defines the module isomorphism $\eta_{W,U}$. The morphism formula in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] shows naturality: both sides of its naturality square are $f_{V\to T}$. For an identity inclusion the component is the identity. For a further open $Z\subseteq W$, every component along either parenthesization of the three restrictions is $1_{F(V\to T)}$ for $V\to Z$; their scalar actions agree by applying the coefficient cocycle twice. The two composites are consequently equal, proving associativity.
